sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《Dealbook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》。

sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的Dealbook峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的人物，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·

sentences.zh: 拉加德、佐兰·蒙达尼以及其他许多人。

sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话实况。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今天。

sentences.en: Facial recognition is becoming an increasingly popular tool for solving crimes.
sentences.zh: 人脸识别正成为一种越来越流行的破案工具。

sentences.en: The Daily's Annie Brown speaks to Kashmir Hill about how that software is not treating everybody equally.
sentences.zh: 《每日新闻》的安妮·布朗采访了克什米尔·希尔，探讨了这种软件为何不能平等地对待所有人。

sentences.en: It's Monday, August 3rd.
sentences.zh: 今天是8月3日，星期一。

sentences.en: I'm just going to tape record with an app that I use.
sentences.zh: 我打算用我常用的一个应用程序来录音。

sentences.en: Do you guys have any questions or concerns before we start talking about what happened?
sentences.zh: 在我们开始谈论发生的事情之前，你们有什么问题或顾虑吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So where do you think we should start the story of this case, Kashmir?
sentences.zh: 那么，克什米尔，你认为我们应该从哪里开始讲这个案子的故事呢？

sentences.en: The story started for the Williams family in January of 2020.
sentences.zh: 对于威廉姆斯一家来说，故事始于2020年1月。

sentences.en: Melissa got the call firSt. I got the call firSt.
sentences.zh: 梅丽莎先接到的电话。是我先接到的电话。

sentences.en: It's a Thursday afternoon in Farmington Hills, Michigan, which is just outside of Detroit.
sentences.zh: 那是一个周四的下午，地点在密歇根州的法明顿希尔斯，就在底特律郊外。

sentences.en: So I picked up Julia from school, regular Thursday.
sentences.zh: 我像往常周四一样，去学校接了朱莉娅。

sentences.en: And Melissa Williams, a realtor, is driving home from work.
sentences.zh: 房地产经纪人梅丽莎·威廉姆斯正开车下班回家。

sentences.en: She's picking up her daughter.
sentences.zh: 她要去接女儿。

sentences.en: And so it was right around like four o'clock.
sentences.zh: 当时大约是四点钟左右。

sentences.en: And I got a call.
sentences.zh: 我接到了一个电话。

sentences.en: And she gets a call from somebody who says they're a police officer.
sentences.zh: 她接到一个自称是警察的人打来的电话。

sentences.en: They immediately said, we're calling about Robert from an incident in 2018.
sentences.zh: 他们直接说，我们是关于2018年的一起事件给罗伯特打电话的。

sentences.en: He needs to turn himself in.
sentences.zh: 他需要自首。

sentences.en: So I was confused off the bat.
sentences.zh: 所以我一开始就很困惑。

sentences.en: She is white.
sentences.zh: 她是白人。

sentences.en: And her husband, Robert Williams, is black.
sentences.zh: 而她的丈夫罗伯特·威廉姆斯是黑人。

sentences.en: And they said, we assume you're his baby mama or that you're not together anymore.
sentences.zh: 他们说，我们以为你是他的孩子他妈，或者你们已经不在一起了。

sentences.en: And I said, that's my husband.
sentences.zh: 我说，那是我丈夫。

sentences.en: And what is this regarding?
sentences.zh: 这到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: And they said, we can't tell you what he needs to come turn himself in.
sentences.zh: 他们说，我们不能告诉你他为什么要来自首。

sentences.en: And I said, well, why didn't you call him?
sentences.zh: 我说，好吧，那你们为什么不直接给他打电话？

sentences.en: And they said, can't you just give him a message?
sentences.zh: 他们说，你不能帮我们传个话吗？

sentences.en: Wait, so why is this officer calling her?
sentences.zh: 等等，那为什么这个警察要给她打电话？

sentences.en: She doesn't know why the officer is calling her.
sentences.zh: 她不知道警察为什么要给她打电话。

sentences.en: All she knows is that the police want to be in touch with her husband.
sentences.zh: 她只知道警察想联系她丈夫。

sentences.en: So she gives the officer her husband's number.
sentences.zh: 于是她把丈夫的号码给了警察。

sentences.en: And then she calls Robert.
sentences.zh: 然后她给罗伯特打了电话。

sentences.en: And I said, I just got a really weird call.
sentences.zh: 我说，我刚才接到了一个非常奇怪的电话。

sentences.en: I was like, what did you do?
sentences.zh: 我问，你做了什么？

sentences.en: Like, what is this about?
sentences.zh: 这到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: And while they're talking, Robert Williams gets a call from the police department.
sentences.zh: 就在他们通话时，罗伯特·威廉姆斯接到了警察局的电话。

sentences.en: Of course, I answered the other line and said he was a detective from Detroit and that I need to come turn myself in.
sentences.zh: 当然，我接了另一条线，他说他是底特律的侦探，我需要去自首。

sentences.en: So of course, I'm like, for what?
sentences.zh: 我当然问，因为什么？

sentences.en: And he's like, well, I can't tell you over the phone.
sentences.zh: 他说，电话里没法告诉你。

sentences.en: So I'm like, well, I can't turn myself in then.
sentences.zh: 我说，那我就没法自首了。

sentences.en: It was a couple of days before his birthday.
sentences.zh: 当时离他生日还有几天。

sentences.en: So he thought maybe it was a prank call.
sentences.zh: 所以他以为这可能是一个恶作剧电话。

sentences.en: But it became pretty clear that the person was serious about probably 10 minutes later,
sentences.zh: 但大约10分钟后，很明显对方是认真的，

sentences.en: I pull in the driveway.
sentences.zh: 我把车开进了车道。

sentences.en: And when he pulls into his driveway, a police car pulls in behind him, blocking him in and two officers get out.
sentences.zh: 当他把车开进自家车道时，一辆警车跟在他后面，挡住了他的去路，两名警察走了出来。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So I get out the car and the driver runs up and he's like, he's like, are you Robert Williams?
sentences.zh: 我下了车，司机跑过来问，你是罗伯特·威廉姆斯吗？

sentences.en: I'm like, yeah.
sentences.zh: 我说，是啊。

sentences.en: He's like, you're under arreSt. I'm like, no, I'm not.
sentences.zh: 他说，你被捕了。我说，不，我没有。

sentences.en: And the guy comes over like a white sheet of paper and it said felony warrant on the top, larceny.
sentences.zh: 那个人拿出一张白纸，上面写着重罪逮捕令，盗窃罪。

sentences.en: And I'm, and I'm like, I'm confused.
sentences.zh: 我当时很困惑。

sentences.en: Like, I'm like, well, isn't larceny stealing?
sentences.zh: 我说，盗窃不就是偷东西吗？

sentences.en: His wife comes out with his two young daughters and his oldest daughter, who's five, is watching this happen.
sentences.zh: 他的妻子带着两个年幼的女儿走了出来，他五岁的大女儿正在看着这一幕发生。

sentences.en: I said, do you go back in the house?
sentences.zh: 我说，你能不能先回屋里去？

sentences.en: I'll be back in a minute.
sentences.zh: 我一会儿就回来。

sentences.en: They just making a mistake.
sentences.zh: 他们只是搞错了。

sentences.en: The guy, the other cop is behind me with his handcuffs out already.
sentences.zh: 另一个人，另一个警察已经在我身后拿出了手铐。

sentences.en: So he's like, come on, man.
sentences.zh: 他说，来吧，伙计。

sentences.en: You are, you know the drill.
sentences.zh: 你知道规矩的。

sentences.en: And I'm like, what?
sentences.zh: 我说，什么？

sentences.en: The officers arrest him.
sentences.zh: 警察逮捕了他。

sentences.en: They have to use two pairs of handcuffs to get his hands behind his back because he's a really big guy.
sentences.zh: 他们不得不用了两副手铐才把他的手反铐在背后，因为他个子非常大。

sentences.en: We started moving seats around, trying to get me in the back of this little bitty Impala.
sentences.zh: 我们开始挪动座位，试图把我塞进这辆小小的英帕拉轿车后座。

sentences.en: And off we go.
sentences.zh: 然后我们就出发了。

sentences.en: And then they drive to the detention center.
sentences.zh: 他们开车把他带到了拘留中心。

sentences.en: I took fingerprints.
sentences.zh: 我采集了指纹。

sentences.en: I took your mugshot.
sentences.zh: 我拍了你的入案照。

sentences.en: Mugshot pictures.
sentences.zh: 入案照片。

sentences.en: Then he's put in a cell to sleep overnight.
sentences.zh: 然后他被关进牢房过夜。

sentences.en: At this point, I'm at a holding sale with two other guys.
sentences.zh: 此时，我正待在一个拘留室里，里面还有另外两个人。

sentences.en: And they're like, what you in here for?
sentences.zh: 他们问，你是因为什么进来的？

sentences.en: And I'm like, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我说，我不知道。

sentences.en: So when do you actually find out why you've been arrested beyond this kind of vague Larson?
sentences.zh: 那么，除了这种模糊的“盗窃罪”，你到底是什么时候才知道自己为什么被捕的？

sentences.en: So maybe like noon the next day?
sentences.zh: 大概是第二天中午吧？

sentences.en: Around noon the next day, he is taken to an interrogation room.
sentences.zh: 第二天中午左右，他被带到了审讯室。

sentences.en: And there's two detectives there.
sentences.zh: 里面有两名侦探。

sentences.en: And they have three pieces of paper face down in front of them.
sentences.zh: 他们面前放着三张反扣着的纸。

sentences.en: And they turn over, you know, the first sheet of paper.
sentences.zh: 他们翻开了第一张纸。

sentences.en: And it's a picture from a surveillance video of a large black man standing in a store wearing a red cardinal's cap and a black jacket.
sentences.zh: 那是一张监控视频截图，显示一个身材高大的黑人男子站在店里，戴着红色的红雀队棒球帽，穿着黑色夹克。

sentences.en: And the detectives ask, is this you?
sentences.zh: 侦探问，这是你吗？

sentences.en: I laugh a little bit and I say, no, that's not me.
sentences.zh: 我笑了一下说，不，那不是我。

sentences.en: So then he turns over another paper.
sentences.zh: 于是他又翻开了另一张纸。

sentences.en: And they turn over a second piece of paper, which is just a close up of that same guy's face.
sentences.zh: 他们翻开了第二张纸，那只是那个人的面部特写。

sentences.en: And he says, I guess that's not you either.
sentences.zh: 他说，我想那也不是你吧。

sentences.en: And I said, no, this is not me.
sentences.zh: 我说，不，这也不是我。

sentences.en: So Robert picks the piece of paper up, holds it next to his own face.
sentences.zh: 于是罗伯特拿起那张纸，放在自己脸旁边比对。

sentences.en: I was like, what do you think all black men look alike?
sentences.zh: 我说，你们是不是觉得所有黑人长得都一样？

sentences.en: And says, do all black men look the same to you?
sentences.zh: 并说，在你们眼里所有黑人都长得一样吗？

sentences.en: So what's your understanding, Kashmir, of what happened to bring Robert Williams into that police department?
sentences.zh: 那么克什米尔，你对导致罗伯特·威廉姆斯被带进警察局的原因有什么了解？

sentences.en: So Robert Williams had no idea what was happening.
sentences.zh: 罗伯特·威廉姆斯根本不知道发生了什么。

sentences.en: But two years earlier in October
sentences.zh: 但在两年前的10月，

sentences.en: 2018, a man who was not him walked into a Shinola store in downtown Detroit.
sentences.zh: 2018年，一个不是他的人走进了一家位于底特律市中心的Shinola商店。

sentences.en: And Shinola is kind of like a high end store that sells expensive watches and bikes.
sentences.zh: Shinola是一家高端商店，出售昂贵的手表和自行车。

sentences.en: And so this man came in, he was there for a few minutes.
sentences.zh: 那个人进去了，待了几分钟。

sentences.en: He stole five watches worth $3,800 and walked out.
sentences.zh: 他偷走了五块价值3800美元的手表，然后走了出去。

sentences.en: None of the employees there actually saw the theft occur.
sentences.zh: 那里的员工实际上没有人看到盗窃发生的过程。

sentences.en: And so they had to review the surveillance footage and they found the moment it happened.
sentences.zh: 所以他们不得不查看监控录像，并找到了事发的那一刻。

sentences.en: So they sent that surveillance footage picture that Robert Williams had been shown to the
sentences.zh: 于是他们把罗伯特·威廉姆斯被展示的那张监控录像截图发给了

sentences.en: Detroit police.
sentences.zh: 底特律警方。

sentences.en: And the police turned to what a lot of police turn to these days when they have a suspect that they don't recognize, a facial recognition system.
sentences.zh: 警方求助于如今许多警察在认不出嫌疑人时会使用的工具：人脸识别系统。

sentences.en: So they ran a search on this, what they call a probe image, this picture for the surveillance video, which is really grainy.
sentences.zh: 他们对这张所谓的“探测图像”进行了搜索，也就是那张来自监控视频的照片，图像非常模糊。

sentences.en: It's not a very good photo.
sentences.zh: 那不是一张很好的照片。

sentences.en: And the way these systems work is that they have access not just to mugshots, but also to driver's license photos.
sentences.zh: 这些系统的工作方式是，它们不仅能访问入案照片，还能访问驾照照片。

sentences.en: You get a bunch of different results and there's a human involved who decides which of the results looks the most like the person who committed the crime.
sentences.zh: 你会得到一堆不同的结果，然后会有专人参与，决定哪个结果看起来最像犯罪嫌疑人。

sentences.en: So you're saying the facial recognition algorithm basically created a lineup of potential suspects.
sentences.zh: 所以你是说人脸识别算法基本上创建了一个潜在嫌疑人的排查名单。

sentences.en: And then from that lineup, someone picks the person that they think looks the most like the man in the surveillance video.
sentences.zh: 然后从那个名单中，有人挑选出他们认为看起来最像监控视频中那个男人的照片。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so that is how they wound up arresting Robert WilliaMs.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们最终逮捕罗伯特·威廉姆斯的原因。

sentences.en: So back in this room, the two detectives now have the real Robert Williams in front of them and he doesn't look like this guy.
sentences.zh: 回到审讯室，两名侦探现在面对的是真正的罗伯特·威廉姆斯，他长得并不像那个人。

sentences.en: You know, they sat back and looked at each other and was like, with the oops face.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们靠在椅背上看着对方，露出了那种“哎呀”的表情。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I said, so I guess the computer got it wrong, too.
sentences.zh: 我说，看来电脑也搞错了。

sentences.en: And so they kind of leaned back and said, I guess the computer got it wrong.
sentences.zh: 他们靠在椅背上说，我想电脑确实搞错了。

sentences.en: Well, the computer got it wrong is what threw me off.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那句“电脑搞错了”让我感到非常意外。

sentences.en: And I'm like, the computer got it wrong.
sentences.zh: 我说，电脑搞错了。

sentences.en: And what is the significance of that statement, that the computer got it wrong?
sentences.zh: 那么，“电脑搞错了”这句话有什么意义呢？

sentences.en: So this was an admission by the detectives that it was a computer that had pointed the finger at
sentences.zh: 这是侦探们承认是电脑指认了

sentences.en: Robert WilliaMs. And that's significant because this is the first documented case of an innocent person being arrested because of a flawed facial recognition match.
sentences.zh: 罗伯特·威廉姆斯。这意义重大，因为这是首例有记录的因人脸识别匹配错误而导致无辜者被捕的案件。

sentences.en: And just to put all of this into context for a second, the last time that you and I talked,
sentences.zh: 为了让这一切有个背景，上次你和我交谈时，

sentences.en: Kashmir, we were talking about a different development in facial recognition.
sentences.zh: 克什米尔，我们谈到了人脸识别领域的另一项进展。

sentences.en: This new algorithm being used by some police departments that drew from pictures all over social media and all over the internet to make a kind of super algorithm.
sentences.zh: 一些警察部门正在使用一种新的算法，它从社交媒体和互联网上的所有照片中提取信息，从而制造出一种“超级算法”。

sentences.en: But the fear wasn't that it wasn't accurate.
sentences.zh: 但人们担心的并不是它不准确。

sentences.en: It was almost that it was too accurate, that it knew too much.
sentences.zh: 而是它几乎太准确了，知道得太多了。

sentences.en: But what you're describing is something altogether different, right?
sentences.zh: 但你所描述的是完全不同的东西，对吧？

sentences.en: So when we talk about facial recognition, we often think of it as a monolith, that there's kind of one facial recognition.
sentences.zh: 当我们谈论人脸识别时，我们通常认为它是一个整体，认为只有一种人脸识别技术。

sentences.en: But in fact, there's a bunch of different companies that all have their own algorithMs. And some work well, and some don't work well.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，有许多不同的公司，它们都有各自的算法。有些效果很好，有些则不然。

sentences.en: And some work well, sometimes like identifying a really clear photo is a lot easier than identifying surveillance footage.
sentences.zh: 有些在某些情况下效果很好，比如识别一张非常清晰的照片比识别监控录像要容易得多。

sentences.en: And why wouldn't police departments be using the most sophisticated, the most kind of up-to-date version of this software?
sentences.zh: 那为什么警察部门不使用最先进、最前沿的软件版本呢？

sentences.en: I mean, this is where you run into just bureaucracy, right?
sentences.zh: 这就是官僚主义作祟的地方，对吧？

sentences.en: You have contracts with companies that go back years, and just a lot of different vendors.
sentences.zh: 你与公司签订的合同可以追溯到几年前，而且供应商也非常多。

sentences.en: And so in this case, I tried to figure out exactly whose algorithms were responsible for Robert Williams getting arrested.
sentences.zh: 所以在这个案子里，我试图弄清楚到底是谁的算法导致了罗伯特·威廉姆斯的被捕。

sentences.en: And I had to really dig down and I discovered the police had no idea, you know, they contract out to a company called DataWorks Plus.
sentences.zh: 我深入挖掘后发现，警方根本不知道，他们外包给了一家叫DataWorks Plus的公司。

sentences.en: And DataWorks Plus contracts out to two other companies called NEC and Rank One actually supply the algorithm.
sentences.zh: 而DataWorks Plus又将业务外包给了另外两家公司，分别是NEC和Rank One，实际上是它们提供了算法。

sentences.en: It's this whole chain of companies that are involved.
sentences.zh: 这涉及一整条公司链条。

sentences.en: And there's no standardized testing.
sentences.zh: 而且没有标准化的测试。

sentences.en: There's no one really regulating this.
sentences.zh: 实际上没有人对此进行监管。

sentences.en: There's just nobody saying which algorithms, you know, pass the test to be used by law enforcement.
sentences.zh: 根本没人说明哪些算法通过了测试，可以供执法部门使用。

sentences.en: It's just up to police officers who, for the most part, seem to be just testing it in the field to see if it works, if it's identifying the right people.
sentences.zh: 这完全取决于警官，他们大多似乎只是在实地测试，看看它是否有效，是否能识别出正确的人。

sentences.en: But the really big problem is that these systems have been proven to be biased.
sentences.zh: 但真正的大问题是，这些系统已被证明存在偏见。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: So Kashmir, help me understand how an algorithm can become biased.
sentences.zh: 那么克什米尔，帮我理解一下算法是如何产生偏见的。

sentences.en: Well, the bias tends to come from how the algorithm is trained.
sentences.zh: 嗯，偏见往往源于算法的训练方式。

sentences.en: And these algorithms tend to be trained by basically feeding them with a bunch of images of people.
sentences.zh: 这些算法通常是通过向它们输入大量人物图像来进行训练的。

sentences.en: But the problem with the algorithms is that they tended to be trained with non-diverse data sets.
sentences.zh: 但这些算法的问题在于，它们往往是用非多样化的数据集进行训练的。

sentences.en: So one good example is that many of the algorithms used by law enforcement in the U.S., by government in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 一个很好的例子是，美国执法部门和政府使用的许多算法，

sentences.en: are very good at recognizing white men and not as good at recognizing black people or Asian Americans.
sentences.zh: 它们非常擅长识别白人男性，但在识别黑人或亚裔美国人时表现却没那么好。

sentences.en: But if you go to an algorithm from a company in China where they fed it with a lot of images of
sentences.zh: 但如果你使用中国公司开发的算法，他们输入了大量

sentences.en: Asian people, they're really good at recognizing Asian people and not as good at recognizing white men.
sentences.zh: 亚洲人的图像，那么它们在识别亚洲人方面非常出色，而在识别白人男性时表现就没那么好。

sentences.en: And so you can just, you can see the biases that come in from the kind of data that we feed into these systeMs.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以看到，我们输入到这些系统中的数据类型带来了偏见。

sentences.en: And is this a widely agreed upon reality that because of these methods, the algorithms used in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 那么，这是否是一个被广泛认可的事实：由于这些方法，美国使用的算法

sentences.en: are just worse at identifying faces that aren't white men?
sentences.zh: 在识别非白人男性面孔时表现更差？

sentences.en: Yeah, a few years ago, an MIT researcher did this study and found that facial recognition algorithms were biased to be able to recognize white men better.
sentences.zh: 是的，几年前，一位麻省理工学院的研究人员做了一项研究，发现人脸识别算法存在偏见，能更好地识别白人男性。

sentences.en: And shortly after that, NIST, the National
sentences.zh: 在那之后不久，美国国家标准与技术研究院（NIST）

sentences.en: Institute of Standards and Technology, decided to run its own study on this.
sentences.zh: 决定对此进行自己的研究。

sentences.en: And it found the same thing.
sentences.zh: 结果发现了同样的情况。

sentences.en: It looked at over 100 different algorithms and it found that they were biased.
sentences.zh: 它考察了100多种不同的算法，发现它们都存在偏见。

sentences.en: And actually, the two algorithms that were at the heart of this case, at Robert Williams' case, were in that study.
sentences.zh: 事实上，本案核心的那两个算法，也就是罗伯特·威廉姆斯的案件，就在那项研究中。

sentences.en: So the algorithm that was used by this police department was actually studied by the federal government and was proven to be biased against faces like Robert WilliaMs.
sentences.zh: 所以，该警察局使用的算法实际上经过了联邦政府的研究，并被证明对罗伯特·威廉姆斯这类面孔存在偏见。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So given these widely understood problems with these algorithms, how can police departments justify continuing to use them?
sentences.zh: 既然这些算法存在广为人知的问题，警察局怎么能证明继续使用它们是合理的呢？

sentences.en: So police departments are aware of the bias problem, but they feel that face recognition is just too valuable a tool in their tool set to solve crimes.
sentences.zh: 警察局确实意识到了偏见问题，但他们认为人脸识别是他们工具箱中解决犯罪过于宝贵的工具。

sentences.en: And their defense is that they never arrest somebody based on facial recognition alone.
sentences.zh: 他们的辩解是，他们绝不会仅凭人脸识别就逮捕某人。

sentences.en: That facial recognition is only what they call an investigative lead.
sentences.zh: 人脸识别只是他们所说的调查线索。

sentences.en: It doesn't supply probable cause for arreSt. So what police are supposed to do is they get a facial recognition match and you're supposed to do more investigating.
sentences.zh: 它不能提供逮捕的合理依据。所以警察应该做的是，在获得人脸识别匹配结果后，进行更多的调查。

sentences.en: So you could go to the person's, you know, social media account and see if there are other photos of them wearing the
sentences.zh: 比如你可以查看那个人的社交媒体账户，看看是否有他们穿着

sentences.en: same clothes that they were wearing on the day they committed this crime.
sentences.zh: 犯罪当天所穿衣服的其他照片。

sentences.en: Or, you know, you can try to get proof that they were in that part of town on the day that the theft occurred.
sentences.zh: 或者，你可以尝试获取证据，证明他们在盗窃发生的当天出现在城镇的那一区域。

sentences.en: You know, try to get location data.
sentences.zh: 你知道，尝试获取位置数据。

sentences.en: Basically find other evidence that this person is the person that committed the crime.
sentences.zh: 基本上就是寻找其他证据，证明此人就是犯罪者。

sentences.en: The detectives just went to the woman who had spotted the theft on the video and showed her a photo of six people.
sentences.zh: 侦探们只是找到了在视频中发现盗窃案的那位女士，并向她展示了一张六人照片。

sentences.en: They called a six pack.
sentences.zh: 他们称之为“六人排查”。

sentences.en: And she said, Robert Williams looked the most like the person that was in the video.
sentences.zh: 她说，罗伯特·威廉姆斯看起来最像视频里的人。

sentences.en: So they're supposed to use the facial recognition match as a kind of clue.
sentences.zh: 所以他们应该把人脸识别匹配结果当作一种线索。

sentences.en: And then the protocol calls for them to do more police work to verify it.
sentences.zh: 然后程序要求他们进行更多的警务工作来核实它。

sentences.en: But in this case, they basically just had someone watch the video and then identify
sentences.zh: 但在本案中，他们基本上只是让某人看了视频，然后指认

sentences.en: Robert Williams as the one who looks most like the guy in the video.
sentences.zh: 罗伯特·威廉姆斯是看起来最像视频里那个人的人。

sentences.en: Yeah, they just did facial recognition a second time, but with a human who's not actually trained.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们只是进行了第二次人脸识别，但这次是由一个未经训练的人来完成的。

sentences.en: And they didn't do any other investigating.
sentences.zh: 而且他们没有做任何其他调查。

sentences.en: Based on that, they went out and they arrested Mr. WilliaMs.
sentences.zh: 基于此，他们就出去逮捕了威廉姆斯先生。

sentences.en: But if the police had done their job correctly, if they had looked into his social media accounts,
sentences.zh: 但如果警察正确地履行了职责，如果他们调查了他的社交媒体账户，

sentences.en: if they had tried to get his location data from his phone records, essentially surveilling him more closely, wouldn't that be its own sort of violation?
sentences.zh: 如果他们试图从他的手机记录中获取位置数据，本质上是更密切地监视他，这难道不是一种侵犯吗？

sentences.en: Just because their technology wrongfully identified this man, he gets more closely watched by the police without his knowledge.
sentences.zh: 仅仅因为他们的技术错误地识别了这个男人，他就被警察在不知情的情况下更密切地监视了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And this is actually what police asked the facial recognition vendors to do.
sentences.zh: 而这实际上正是警察要求人脸识别供应商去做的事情。

sentences.en: They want to have more what you call false positives, because they want to have the greatest pool of possible suspects that they can because they want to find the bad guy.
sentences.zh: 他们想要更多的所谓“假阳性”，因为他们想要尽可能多地获得潜在嫌疑人，因为他们想找到坏人。

sentences.en: But there is there's a real toll from that.
sentences.zh: 但这确实带来了真正的代价。

sentences.en: I just, you know, as a person who's been reporting on technology for a decade, I just think people trust computers.
sentences.zh: 我只是，作为一个报道科技行业十年的记者，我认为人们信任计算机。

sentences.en: And even when we know something is flawed, if it's a computer telling us to do it, we just think it's right.
sentences.zh: 即使我们知道某样东西有缺陷，如果是计算机告诉我们去做，我们就会认为它是对的。

sentences.en: And this is why we always used to see for a long time, when mapping technology was first being developed, and it wasn't that great.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我们过去很长一段时间里总是看到，当地图技术刚开始开发时，它还不是那么好。

sentences.en: You know, people would drive into lakes, they would drive over cliffs, because a mapping app said, you're supposed to go straight here, right?
sentences.zh: 人们会开车冲进湖里，会开车冲下悬崖，因为地图应用说，你应该直走，对吧？

sentences.en: And even though they could look and see that their life is going to be in danger, they would think, well, this app must know what it's talking about.
sentences.zh: 即使他们能看到自己的生命将处于危险之中，他们也会想，嗯，这个应用一定知道它在说什么。

sentences.en: That's facial recognition now.
sentences.zh: 现在的人脸识别也是如此。

sentences.en: And when I was reporting the story, all the experts I talked to said, this is surely not the first case where somebody has been mistakenly, an
sentences.zh: 当我报道这个故事时，我采访的所有专家都说，这肯定不是第一个有人被错误地、一个

sentences.en: innocent person has been mistakenly arrested because of a bad face recognition match.
sentences.zh: 无辜的人因为糟糕的人脸识别匹配而被错误逮捕的案例。

sentences.en: But usually people don't find out about it.
sentences.zh: 但通常人们不会发现这一点。

sentences.en: Police don't tell people that they're there because of face recognition.
sentences.zh: 警察不会告诉人们他们是因为人脸识别才被抓的。

sentences.en: You know, usually when they charge them, they'll just say they were identified through investigative means.
sentences.zh: 通常当他们指控他们时，只会说他们是通过调查手段被识别出来的。

sentences.en: It's kind of a vague, there were clues that pointed at you.
sentences.zh: 这是一种模糊的说法，就是有线索指向了你。

sentences.en: In that way, Robert's case was unusual, because there was so little evidence against him.
sentences.zh: 从这个角度看，罗伯特的案子很不寻常，因为针对他的证据太少了。

sentences.en: It basically had to tell him that they use facial recognition, you know, to put him there.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上不得不告诉他，他们使用了人脸识别才把他抓到这里。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: They showed him what most people don't get to see, which is this false match between his photo and the photo of the crime.
sentences.zh: 他们向他展示了大多数人看不到的东西，也就是他的照片和犯罪照片之间的错误匹配。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And what's happened since Robert was arrested?
sentences.zh: 罗伯特被捕后发生了什么？

sentences.en: So Robert had to hire a lawyer to defend himself.
sentences.zh: 罗伯特不得不聘请律师为自己辩护。

sentences.en: But when he went to the hearing,
sentences.zh: 但当他去参加听证会时，

sentences.en: the prosecutor decided to drop the case.
sentences.zh: 检察官决定撤销此案。

sentences.en: But they dropped it without prejudice, which meant that they could charge him again.
sentences.zh: 但他们撤销时没有附带“不得再诉”的条件，这意味着他们可以再次起诉他。

sentences.en: For the same crime?
sentences.zh: 因为同样的罪名？

sentences.en: With the same crime.
sentences.zh: 同样的罪名。

sentences.en: So as I was reporting out the story, you know, I went to the prosecutor's office, I went to the Detroit Police Department, and I said, you know, what happened here?
sentences.zh: 所以当我在报道这个故事时，我去了检察官办公室，去了底特律警察局，我说，这里发生了什么？

sentences.en: Did you have any other evidence?
sentences.zh: 你们还有其他证据吗？

sentences.en: It just seems like a clear misfire and misuse of facial recognition.
sentences.zh: 这看起来显然是人脸识别的失误和滥用。

sentences.en: And everyone involved was pretty defensive and said, well, you know, there might be more evidence that proves that Robert Williams did it.
sentences.zh: 所有相关人员都相当抵触，说，嗯，可能还有更多证据证明是罗伯特·威廉姆斯干的。

sentences.en: But after the story came out, everybody's tune changed dramatically.
sentences.zh: 但在报道出来后，所有人的态度都发生了巨大的转变。

sentences.en: Prosecutor's office apologized, said that Robert Williams shouldn't have spent any time in jail.
sentences.zh: 检察官办公室道歉了，说罗伯特·威廉姆斯本不该在监狱里待上一分钟。

sentences.en: The Detroit Police Department said this was a horrible investigation.
sentences.zh: 底特律警察局说这是一次糟糕的调查。

sentences.en: The police officers involved just did this all wrong.
sentences.zh: 涉案警官完全做错了。

sentences.en: This isn't how it's supposed to work.
sentences.zh: 这不应该是这样的运作方式。

sentences.en: And they said that Robert
sentences.zh: 他们说罗伯特·威廉姆斯

sentences.en: Williams would have his information expunged from the system, his mugshot, his DNA.
sentences.zh: 的信息将从系统中删除，包括他的入案照和DNA。

sentences.en: And they personally apologized to the Williams family, though the Williams family told me that no one ever actually called them to personally apologize.
sentences.zh: 他们亲自向威廉姆斯一家道歉，尽管威廉姆斯一家告诉我，从来没有人真正打电话给他们亲自道歉。

sentences.en: But he can no longer be charged in the future for this crime.
sentences.zh: 但他以后不能再因这起罪名被起诉了。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And what about their use of facial recognition software?
sentences.zh: 那么他们对人脸识别软件的使用呢？

sentences.en: Has there been any change there?
sentences.zh: 那方面有什么变化吗？

sentences.en: So one thing that the Detroit Police Department said was, well, this was, you know, this was a case that predates this new policy we have that says, you know, we're only
sentences.zh: 底特律警察局说的一件事是，嗯，这是一个早于我们新政策的案例，新政策规定，我们只

sentences.en: supposed to be using facial recognition for violent crimes.
sentences.zh: 应该将人脸识别用于暴力犯罪。

sentences.en: And what do you make of that?
sentences.zh: 你对此怎么看？

sentences.en: Why only use this tool for that?
sentences.zh: 为什么只把这个工具用于那种情况？

sentences.en: Well, their justification is that when it comes to violent crimes, when it comes to murder, you know,
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们的理由是，当涉及到暴力犯罪时，当涉及到谋杀、强奸时，

sentences.en: rape, they need to solve these cases and they'll use any clue they can to do it, including facial recognition.
sentences.zh: 他们需要破案，他们会利用任何能利用的线索，包括人脸识别。

sentences.en: But I think about something that Robert's wife said.
sentences.zh: 但我想到罗伯特的妻子说的一件事。

sentences.en: When they pulled up to our house, they were already combative on the phone.
sentences.zh: 当他们开车到我们家时，他们在电话里就已经很有敌意了。

sentences.en: They were aggressive in the doorway to me.
sentences.zh: 他们在门口对我表现得很激进。

sentences.en: What if he had been argumentative?
sentences.zh: 如果他当时争辩了呢？

sentences.en: If he'd been defensive?
sentences.zh: 如果他当时防卫了呢？

sentences.en: He hadn't complied.
sentences.zh: 如果他没有配合呢？

sentences.en: You know, what could that have turned into in our yard?
sentences.zh: 你知道，在我们的院子里会变成什么样？

sentences.en: Like,
sentences.zh: 就像，

sentences.en: it could have went a different way.
sentences.zh: 事情可能会走向另一个方向。

sentences.en: And the recent news has shown us that it definitely could have went a different way.
sentences.zh: 最近的新闻向我们表明，它绝对可能走向另一个方向。

sentences.en: Do you feel like there's a shame to this, that the police arrested you, even though you did nothing?
sentences.zh: 你觉得这是一种耻辱吗？警察逮捕了你，尽管你什么都没做？

sentences.en: It's a little humiliating.
sentences.zh: 这有点丢人。

sentences.en: It's, you know, it's not a, it's not something easily rolls off the tongue.
sentences.zh: 这，你知道，这不是一件容易说出口的事情。

sentences.en: Like, oh yeah, and guess what?
sentences.zh: 就像，哦，对了，你猜怎么着？

sentences.en: I got arrested.
sentences.zh: 我被捕了。

sentences.en: And what about for Robert himself?
sentences.zh: 那罗伯特本人呢？

sentences.en: What has life been like for him after the arrest?
sentences.zh: 他被捕后的生活是怎样的？

sentences.en: So this was very embarrassing for him.
sentences.zh: 这对他是非常尴尬的。

sentences.en: It's kind of painful in some ways.
sentences.zh: 在某些方面这很痛苦。

sentences.en: So he had a perfect attendance at work until that day that he was arrested and his wife had to email his boss and
sentences.zh: 他在被捕那天之前工作全勤，他的妻子不得不给老板发邮件，

sentences.en: say that they had a family emergency and that he couldn't show up that day.
sentences.zh: 说他们家里有急事，他那天不能去上班。

sentences.en: Once he did tell his boss what happened, his boss said, you know, you don't want to tell other people at work, you know, it could be bad for you.
sentences.zh: 一旦他告诉老板发生了什么，老板说，你不想告诉单位里的其他人，这对你可能不好。

sentences.en: The night he got home, his daughter, his five-year-old was still awake.
sentences.zh: 他回家的那天晚上，他的女儿，五岁的孩子还没睡。

sentences.en: Julie was still up and I was like, what are you doing up?
sentences.zh: 朱莉还没睡，我说，你还没睡吗？

sentences.en: And she's like, I'm waiting for you.
sentences.zh: 她说，我在等你。

sentences.en: And I was like, I told you I'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我说，我告诉过你我会马上回来。

sentences.en: And she was like, you didn't come right back though.
sentences.zh: 她说，但你没有马上回来。

sentences.en: So I just kept telling her that they made a mistake and it just took longer than we expected.
sentences.zh: 所以我一直告诉她，他们犯了一个错误，只是比我们预期的花了更长时间。

sentences.en: But, um, she started wanting to play cops and robbers and she would always pretend like he was the robber who stole something and she would need to lock him up in the living room.
sentences.zh: 但是，她开始想玩警察抓小偷的游戏，她总是假装他是偷了东西的强盗，她需要把他锁在客厅里。

sentences.en: Oh yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: She told us that she told one of her jacks and her friend at school and we, we weren't sure.
sentences.zh: 她告诉我们她告诉了学校里的一个朋友，我们不确定。

sentences.en: Did she tell her teacher?
sentences.zh: 她告诉老师了吗？

sentences.en: Did she tell her friends?
sentences.zh: 她告诉朋友了吗？

sentences.en: Did we, we were not sure.
sentences.zh: 我们不确定。

sentences.en: And we didn't know what to say to people like, just bring it up out of nowhere.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道该怎么跟人说，就像，突然提起这件事。

sentences.en: Like, oh yeah.
sentences.zh: 就像，哦，对了。

sentences.en: In case anyone mentioned it, he was arrested, but he didn't do anything.
sentences.zh: 万一有人提到它，他被捕了，但他什么都没做。

sentences.en: Has this made you look back to see where you, like where you were October, 2018?
sentences.zh: 这让你回想过2018年10月你在哪里吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I pulled it up.
sentences.zh: 是的，我查过了。

sentences.en: I was, uh,
sentences.zh: 我当时，呃，

sentences.en: at the time I was on my Facebook or on my Instagram live.
sentences.zh: 当时我正在Facebook或Instagram上直播。

sentences.en: He has since looked back and realized that he had posted to Instagram at basically the same time as the shoplifting was occurring.
sentences.zh: 他后来回想起来，意识到他在商店行窃发生时基本上就在Instagram上发帖。

sentences.en: He was driving home from work and a song came on the radio that his, um, mother loved.
sentences.zh: 他当时正开车下班回家，收音机里放着他母亲喜欢的一首歌。

sentences.en: The song, We Are One by
sentences.zh: 那首歌是《We Are One》，由

sentences.en: Mays and Frankie Beverly.
sentences.zh: 梅斯和弗兰基·贝弗利演唱。

sentences.en: I was singing songs on my way home in the car.
sentences.zh: 我在回家的车上唱着歌。

sentences.en: So if the cops had looked into his social media, if they had tried to verify that it was possible that he could have committed this crime, they could have found this video.
sentences.zh: 所以如果警察调查了他的社交媒体，如果他们试图核实他是否可能犯下这起罪行，他们本可以找到这段视频。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: If the police had done a real investigation, they would have found out he had an alibi that day.
sentences.zh: 如果警察进行了真正的调查，他们就会发现他那天有不在场证明。

sentences.en: Kashmir, thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 克什米尔，非常感谢。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是您今天还需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: Federal unemployment benefits have expired for tens of millions of Americans after Congress failed to reach a deal to renew them last week.
sentences.zh: 由于国会上周未能就延长联邦失业救济金达成协议，数千万美国人的这项福利已经到期。

sentences.en: So what do you say to those 30 million Americans who are now without federal unemployment help?
sentences.zh: 那么，对于那3000万现在失去联邦失业救济的美国人，您有什么想说的吗？

sentences.en: I say to them, talk to President Trump.
sentences.zh: 我想对他们说，去和特朗普总统谈谈。

sentences.en: He's the one who is standing in the way of that.
sentences.zh: 是他阻碍了这项协议的达成。

sentences.en: We have been for the $600.
sentences.zh: 我们一直支持维持600美元的救济金。

sentences.en: They have a $200 proposal, which does not meet the needs of America's working families.
sentences.zh: 他们提出的200美元方案，根本无法满足美国工薪家庭的需求。

sentences.en: In interviews on Sunday with ABC's This Week, House Speaker Nancy
sentences.zh: 在周日接受美国广播公司《本周》节目采访时，众议院议长南希·

sentences.en: Pelosi blamed Republicans for demanding a drastic cut in the weekly benefit, while Treasury Secretary
sentences.zh: 佩洛西指责共和党人要求大幅削减每周的救济金，而财政部长

sentences.en: Steve Mnuchin claimed that the $600 payments risked overpaying unemployed workers.
sentences.zh: 史蒂文·姆努钦则声称，600美元的支付额存在向失业工人多付钱的风险。

sentences.en: So you do think it is a disincentive to find a job if you have that extra $600?
sentences.zh: 所以您确实认为，如果提供额外的600美元，会让人失去找工作的动力吗？

sentences.en: There's no question in certain cases where we're paying people more to stay home than to work, that's created issues in the entire economy.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，在某些情况下，我们支付给人们留在家里的钱比他们工作赚的还多，这在整个经济中造成了问题。

sentences.en: And the Times reports that July was a devastating month for the pandemic in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 据《纽约时报》报道，七月对美国的疫情来说是灾难性的一月。

sentences.en: The country recorded nearly 2 million new infections, twice as many as any previous month.
sentences.zh: 全国记录了近200万例新增感染病例，是之前任何一个月记录的两倍。

sentences.en: I want to be very clear.
sentences.zh: 我想明确一点。

sentences.en: What we're seeing today is different from
sentences.zh: 我们今天所看到的与

sentences.en: March and April.
sentences.zh: 三月和四月的情况不同。

sentences.en: It is extraordinarily widespread.
sentences.zh: 疫情的蔓延极其广泛。

sentences.en: It's into the rural as equal urban areas.
sentences.zh: 它已经深入到农村地区，和城市地区一样严重。

sentences.en: In an interview on Sunday with CNN, Dr. Deborah Birx, a top White House advisor on the pandemic, acknowledged that the United States has failed to contain the virus.
sentences.zh: 在周日接受美国有线电视新闻网采访时，白宫顶级疫情顾问黛博拉·伯克斯博士承认，美国未能遏制住病毒。

sentences.en: And to everybody who lives in a rural area, you are not immune or protected from this virus.
sentences.zh: 对于每一位居住在农村地区的人，你们并非对这种病毒免疫或受到保护。

sentences.en: And that's why we keep saying no matter where you live in America, you need to wear a mask and socially distance, do the personal hygiene.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我们一直强调，无论你住在美国的哪个地方，都需要佩戴口罩、保持社交距离，并做好个人卫生。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直像一台受到严密控制的机器一样运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer, when elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天，选举迎来了一批自称为改革派的人士。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直陷入一场激烈、混乱，有时又令人兴奋的斗争之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在我和莎拉·凯尼格主持的最新一期《地铁》节目中，我们将讲述人们试图维持影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《地铁》节目。
